newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition to choose PM with eye on polls.
newsitem.headline: India coalition to choose PM with eye on polls.

text.p: India's ousted United Front coalition was under pressure from its constituents on Friday to elect a new leader who could lead them into likely early polls, narrowing the choice to three candidates, officials said.

They said the main theatre of the electoral battle would be India's populous Hindi-speaking northern region where the United Front has the right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as its main opponent.

The coalition's main rival in the southern states was the Congress party, which has offered to support a new United Front government after forcing the fall of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a confidence vote last week, alliance officials said.
"With this in view, the next prime minister should be from the north," a senior leader of the influential Left Front told Reuters.
He said the Left Front, which has 52 of the alliance's 178 lawmakers, was opposed to G.K. Moopanar, leader of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party.
Moopanar is a former member of the Congress party from the southern state of Tamil Nadu and is widely regarded as the Congress party's unstated choice to succeed Deve Gowda.
The United Front on Friday authorised southern Andhra Pradesh state Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu to name a new leader after consultations with the senior leaders of the 15-party coalition.

Among the northern Indian candidates in the fray are Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan and Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, United Front officials said.
Left Front officials said there was growing consensus for Mulayam Singh Yadav as the new leader.
"He would be our choice, but any other northern leader with a mass base will be a good candidate," the official said.
The Mulayam Singh Yadav is a former chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state where the BJP recently formed a local government in alliance with a low caste Hindu party.
Uttar Pradesh elects 85 lawmakers to the 545-seat lower house of parliament.
Laloo Prasad Yadav is the chief minister of Bihar, India's second most populous state which sends 54 deputies to parliament.

"Laloo appears to be a weak candidate because of the scandals surrounding his government," a United Front official said, referring to an ongoing federal police probe into the $285 million financial incident in Bihar.

Paswan belongs to the lowest Hindu caste with a strong appeal against both the Congress and the BJP, a useful factor in the looming against the two parties regarded as largely upper caste, officials said.
The search for a new United Front leader was triggered by the Congress decision to withdraw its crucial support for Deve Gowda's 10-month old government, forcing the vote of confidence on April 11.

United Front sources said Naidu's choice of a leader, to be announced either late on Friday or early Saturday, would be determined by two factors -- keeping the 15-party United Front together and preparing it for elections.
If Moopanar gets elected as the new leader, the Left Front will walk out of the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee, a senior Left Front official said.
"If we can't come to a decision, we will go to polls under Deve Gowda as caretaker prime minister," said a leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, a key constituent of the United Front
